newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.20 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.20 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.20 cent weaker Thursday, based on market orders at 1019 EDT, dealers said.
Prices could retreat from the nine-day highs reached Wednesday, after USDA's supply and demand report, and the weekly export and sales data.

USDA raised its estimate for exports in 1996/97 to 7.1 million bales from 7.0 million bales last month. Indeed, the U.S. sold 62,800 bales of old-crop cotton in the week ended June 5, above expectations of about 50,000 bales, USDA said in its weekly export and sales report.
"These are better numbers than we expected," Smith Barney vice president David Brandon, said.

But analysts were disappointed that the USDA reduced China's ending stocks by only 1.7 million bales, from 17.1 million bales. Traders said a more substantial reduction has already been filtered into the market.
"I want to be enthusiastic because of the close yesterday, but it looks like we could open lower," a trader said.
Wednesday, the July cotton contract closed 1.12 cents higher at 73.64 cents a lb after trading from 73.70 to 72.80 cents. New-crop December went out 1.19 cents higher at 76.15 cents.
July's resistance was pegged at 73.90 cents, the high hit June 2, and then at 74.10 cents, where traders expect to uncover buy stops.
